installSteps.text: Alternatively, download Your SimCity 2000. A Whole New Chapter. directly from the official site at https://rs.realm667.com/. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Open the downloaded .dmg and drag the app into Applications. On first launch macOS may refuse to open it as unidentified — right-click the app and choose Open to approve it once.
Check your distribution's package manager first, which is usually the easiest route. Otherwise download the AppImage from the official site, mark it executable and run it.

Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. Your SimCity 2000. A Whole New Chapter. needs roughly small of free disk space.

faq.q: Is Your SimCity 2000. A Whole New Chapter. free?
faq.a: No — Your SimCity 2000. A Whole New Chapter. must be purchased. It's distributed as Free to play.

faq.q: How big is the Your SimCity 2000. A Whole New Chapter. download?
faq.a: Check the official site for current download size and system requirements.

faq.q: What platforms does Your SimCity 2000. A Whole New Chapter. run on?
Do I need an account to play Your SimCity 2000. A Whole New Chapter.?
faq.a: You can download and play without creating an account.

set.tagline: Build a city with night lights, changing weather and a neighbor who can argue over the budget.
set.description: Daniel Gimmer's free OpenSC2K fork adds replacement art and audio, expanded city tools and experimental 2–8 player multiplayer. Bring an owned SimCity 2000 copy if you want its original assets; the included alternatives work without one.

systemRequirements.min: Windows x64 or ARM64, Linux x64 or ARM64, or macOS Intel or Apple Silicon. Official numerical CPU, RAM and GPU minimums are not published. The Windows and Linux packages need a writable folder; large cities need more memory.
systemRequirements.recommended: The developer does not publish a numerical recommended tier. Allow extra memory for large maps and rendering effects; keep a backup of cities made with the beta.

min.notes: The v1.0.0-beta.1 release offers Windows and Linux x64/ARM64 archives and a universal macOS disk image. CPU, RAM and GPU thresholds are not published.

recommended.notes: No numerical recommended tier is published. Very large cities and visual effects need more memory and GPU headroom.

set.launcherInstall.note: First public beta. Packages include replacement graphics, music and sounds, so an owned SimCity 2000 copy is optional. The currently selected Windows/Linux recipe is x64; ARM64 packages exist on the release page but need architecture-aware launcher selection before one-click install is promised for ARM64. macOS package is ad-hoc signed and may require approval in Privacy & Security. Test each platform before promoting this Draft game.

qualityBar.verdict: A city builder that makes the old street grid feel alive again, then invites another mayor to meddle with it.

set.longDescription:
Reticulating Splines begins with the grid you remember: zone land, connect roads and power, fund services, and watch a city find ways to frustrate your tidy plan. Daniel Gimmer built it as an enhanced fork of Nicholas Ochoa's OpenSC2K, an independent reimplementation rather than a patch for the original SimCity 2000 executable. Its strongest changes are visible before you place a single police station. Daylight fades into streetlights, weather moves over the map, and a familiar isometric city gains a sense of time and place.

You can import graphics, sound and data from a SimCity 2000 copy you own. You do not have to: the beta includes alternative replacement packs for artwork, music and sound. That distinction matters. The engine is free, and the bundled alternative assets make it playable without quietly requiring a paid game. Players who want the original presentation can bring their own files; PlayBound does not provide those copyrighted assets.

The builder itself has room to stretch. New cities begin at 128 by 128 tiles, with larger maps available. Terrain tools, service overlays and additional zoom levels help you understand why a district is failing instead of guessing at the cause. The Expanded rules add metropolis rewards and facility upgrades, while Classic remains there for players who want the older rhythm. Seasons, rain, snow and night lighting can be adjusted independently, so the visual additions do not have to change how the single-player simulation plays. JavaScript mods and separate asset packs give tinkerers another path once they know the city beneath them.

The unusual experiment is sharing that city with other people. Two to eight mayors can host or join a LAN or Internet session in cooperative and competitive modes. One machine owns the simulation; the others send commands. The host can set terrain, land price and a password, while guests choose seats and ready up before the city starts. An online directory helps players find hosts, but actual game traffic connects directly to the host over TCP. Router and firewall settings can still matter. This is experimental beta multiplayer, and we have not verified automatic joining from a PlayBound party or a PlayBound-hosted dedicated process.

The current public build is v1.0.0-beta.1 for Windows, macOS and Linux, with an Android package offered separately by the developer. Its desktop packages include the replacement assets. The creator has not published numerical CPU, memory or graphics minimums, and very large cities will ask more of a machine. Keep backups of beta saves. We are interested in the combination of a generous free city builder and a genuinely different social problem: sharing a budget with someone who has their own idea of what the city needs. It stays in Draft until the installer and multiplayer paths have been tested on supported systems.
set.whyWePickedIt: It makes OpenSC2K playable with its own replacement assets, adds unusually thoughtful city presentation, and tries 2–8 player municipal politics. The first public beta and its direct-host networking still need PlayBound testing before release.
set.thatOneThing: Your rival mayor can disagree with your zoning plan while you're both paying for the same city.

installSteps.text: Download and extract the official v1.0.0-beta.1 Windows x64 ZIP into a writable folder. The release page also offers a separate ARM64 build; PlayBound's current recipe targets x64.
Open the official universal macOS disk image, move the app to Applications, and approve its ad-hoc signature in Privacy & Security if macOS asks.
Extract the official v1.0.0-beta.1 Linux x64 tar.gz into a writable folder. The release page also offers a separate ARM64 build; PlayBound's current recipe targets x64.
Start with the included replacement artwork, music and sound. If you own SimCity 2000 and prefer its originals, use the game's import flow to read your own supported files.

firstPlaySteps.text: Create a Classic city to learn zones, roads, utilities and the annual budget; try Expanded rules after you know the basic economy. Back up beta saves before large experiments.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Open Multiplayer in the game's main menu. The host chooses mode, terrain, land price, password and Internet or LAN visibility. Other players find the lobby or connect directly, claim seats and ready up; the host starts the game. The host must accept inbound TCP on its chosen port, default 20000. PlayBound party handoff has not been verified.

faq.q: Do I need to own SimCity 2000?
faq.a: No. The beta includes alternative graphics, music and sound packs. Import original assets only from a supported copy you own.
The developer calls its 2–8 player LAN and Internet multiplayer experimental. Sessions use an in-game host and direct TCP connection; automatic PlayBound party joining has not yet been tested.

faq.q: Does PlayBound host a dedicated server?
faq.a: No separate game-server binary is documented. The repository's server component serves the Internet directory; a player's game process hosts the city simulation.
The developer does not document a physical-controller layout, and PlayBound has not verified a Controls profile.
Official numerical CPU, RAM and GPU minimums are not published. The desktop beta is available for Windows, macOS and Linux; large maps need more resources.

bestFor: City builders who want classic planning with modern presentation
Friends willing to test experimental shared-city multiplayer
notFor: Players seeking a verified dedicated-server deployment
Players requiring a tested physical-controller layout
